page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8124M processor, delivering 72 virtual CPUs across 36 physical cores with hyper-threading. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and includes 24 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its networking capability, offering a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 66,660.83 and a PassMark CPU score of 49,891.05. Memory bandwidth is also in the top tier, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 208.32 GB/sec and write speeds at 90.55 GB/sec. Single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average tier, indicating that workloads must leverage the high core count to maximize efficiency.

While the instance performs well in parallel processing and database operations, it exhibits limitations in specific workloads. LLM text generation speeds are weak, with a medium 7B model producing only 7.23 tokens per second, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. However, its strong database operations score and high network throughput make it suitable for network-bound applications, distributed database nodes, and compute-heavy batch processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU density and 100 Gbps network baseline provide a balanced resource profile for scale-out workloads without the overhead of local storage.
